We present a study of instruction-tuned language models under long-context retrieval settings, showing that accuracy on needle-in-a-haystack tasks degrades non-uniformly as context length grows, with a pronounced drop when relevant information sits near the middle of the input. To address this, we introduce a lightweight positional re-weighting scheme applied during fine-tuning that requires no architectural changes and adds negligible inference overhead. Across five open-weight model families ranging from seven to seventy billion parameters, our method improves mid-context retrieval accuracy by an average of eighteen points while leaving short-context performance unchanged. We release code and checkpoints to support reproducibility.
